title: SOFT M
territory: A compact, sculpted capital M whose deep open cleft gives a human voice a firm, memorable shape.
oneSentenceMeaning: Speech rises, settles and becomes something you can keep, expressed through the first letter of Mluva.
appIdentity: Mluva is open-source dictation and rewriting for Omarchy, named for the Czech word for speech or manner of speaking. It should feel immediately useful, quietly capable and pleasant to return to every day. A person speaks, reviews the recognized source, edits a working version and shapes a draft without losing the original recognition. Exact editable Markdown and visible provider choices make that ease credible. Local and cloud processing are choices within the product; the identity must not imply that every operation stays on the device. The emotional promise is Most delightful dictation for Omarchy, expressed in small moments of relief rather than a performance claim. SOFT M gives this experience a familiar initial with unusual tactile confidence. It belongs beside the disciplined typography of an Omarchy desktop while making room for a warmer, more personal rhythm: A little more delight every day.
markIdentity: The initial study starts with a capital M that feels cut from one soft, dense material. Two substantial outer legs support a low central join. A deep cleft enters from the top, while two generous spaces open upward from the baseline beneath the descending diagonal masses. These three interruptions make the letter readable before any metaphor is explained. The top contour rises and falls like the emphasis of a short spoken phrase, but its overall form remains an initial rather than an audio diagram. Broad, gently changing curves suggest ease; deliberate feet and an upright stance suggest an application that keeps its work in order. The mark should feel approachable without becoming cute, inflated or liquid. It has no enclosing tile, detached particle or decorative interior line. A single solid silhouette must carry its identity in a launcher, a symbolic icon and the opening or closing frame of the film. The study tests whether a memorable M can carry more warmth than the existing abstract unfolding-thought mark.
logoDescription:
Initial study: draw one connected, solid capital M, slightly wider than it is tall. Treat the contour as the boundary of a dense piece of material. Two broad outside legs rise from short, nearly flat feet into rounded shoulders. Between those shoulders, a deep, open central cleft descends into the upper half of the body. The diagonals beneath it merge into a low, softly blunted center. Two open lower bays separate this center from the feet, exposing enough background to make the M immediately legible. The letter has weight, but the openings give it air.

Use almost equal shoulder heights in the first drawing, with the left shoulder marginally fuller. Keep the outer legs near vertical through most of their height, allowing their curves to emerge gradually as they turn over the shoulders. The top cleft should have inclined sides and a rounded floor; it must not become the shallow notch of a lowercase m. The low center stops above the baseline, so the two outside feet are the only parts that stand on it. The bottom openings are shaped by the diagonal masses above them, rather than drilled as matching circular holes.

The first impression should be a calm, confident initial. The second is the physical rhythm of saying a word: an opening, a drop in pitch and a renewed rise. This interpretation comes from the letter's contour and does not require a waveform, literal mouth or speech tail. The silhouette should feel pleasantly handled, with the slight variation of a well-shaped object. Flat monochrome ink supplies all its visual weight; dimensionality must come from the drawing itself.

At large scale, evaluate the balance between the central join and the two outside legs. At twenty-four pixels, evaluate the unmistakable M, the depth of the top cleft and the survival of both lower openings. The initial concept deliberately exposes a difficult question: whether its nearly balanced shoulders and broad curves are distinctive enough to escape the familiar rounded startup monogram. The adversarial review below treats that as a structural issue to resolve before generating the final study. Keep the mark alone on actual transparent alpha, with no background container, lettering, outline, shading or texture.
wordmarkDescription:
Initial study: set the exact name Mluva in title case, beginning with the filled glyph forms of JetBrains Mono Medium. Preserve the family resemblance to the application's editable text, especially its upright rhythm, open counters and practical distinction between letters. Then redraw the name as dedicated artwork. The result should be recognizably related to JetBrains Mono while showing a stronger design decision than ordinary typesetting or a narrowed lowercase l.

The initial M is the main intervention. Broaden it beyond the original monospace cell and replace its rigid diagonal junction with the mark's deep central cleft and low, gently blunted join. Keep it a letter at the same cap height as the original type, with less mass than the standalone symbol so it does not overwhelm the following lowercase forms. Its shoulder turns introduce the curve language used throughout the name. The l becomes narrower but retains a small head flag and a definite rightward foot, preserving its identity beside the M. This pair should feel deliberately spaced, never like a logo followed by four unrelated typed characters.

Carry the same material logic into the u and v. Give the u a generous interior and a broad, softly turning base. Keep the v visibly diagonal, but replace its needle point with a short rounded termination that echoes the M's center. Retain the two-storey a from the typographic starting point; open its upper counter and soften the lower bowl's transition into the right stem. These are changes to the letter skeleton and counter proportions, not a global corner-rounding effect.

Allow optical spacing to replace the monospace grid. Tighten M–l, give l–u enough room to keep the foot distinct, and make u–v and v–a feel equal in perceived area. The wordmark should have one continuous reading rhythm without touching or joining letters. Its warmth comes from deliberate turns and compact spacing. Keep the final artwork as solid filled forms with font provenance retained when it is eventually drawn; the application font itself remains the established JetBrains Mono family.
selfCritique: The initial silhouette is still close to a generic rounded M. Almost equal shoulders and uniformly friendly curves are a category convention, not a sufficiently memorable decision. A larger radius is not an identity.

The first description leaves the top cleft too shallow. At small sizes that could turn the uppercase M into a lowercase m, two arches or a tooth. The revised drawing needs a substantially deeper opening and visibly inclined interior sides.

A thick center can turn into a tongue, a third foot or a soft triangle suspended between the legs. That would pull the mark toward a mouth, a bowtie or an indistinct blob. Its underside must finish clearly above the baseline and remain narrower than the outside legs combined.

Tiny asymmetry is an unreliable signature. If the only distinguishing feature disappears at twenty-four pixels, the concept has not earned its place. Shoulder height, trough placement and foot structure must create a readable overall stance without sacrificing the letter.

The paired lower openings could close under rasterization, particularly in a reversed light version. Attractive large artwork is insufficient evidence. The study needs explicit minimum opening and stem targets, followed by actual pixel review before any adoption.

The initial wordmark risks becoming a custom M attached to nearly stock luva. Rounding the u and v and narrowing the l do not yet establish a coherent signature. The a needs a meaningful proportion change, and the negative spaces must be designed as a family.

A soft M carries no inherent claim about source fidelity, local processing or open source. Those belong to product behavior and surrounding communication. The voice interpretation is an association, not a factual demonstration, and this study has not established trademark uniqueness.
revision:
Final direction: retain the single filled capital M, but replace the nearly symmetric pillow geometry with a more deliberate stance. Set width to approximately 1.06 times height. The left shoulder reaches the full height; the right shoulder sits five percent lower and turns down more quickly into its outside leg. Move the center of the top cleft to fifty-three percent of the width and deepen its floor to fifty-eight percent of the height. Its low interior join ends at eighty-two percent of the height, leaving an unmistakable eighteen-percent lift above the baseline. The cleft and join share an axis. Preserve inclined inner sides and broad outer legs, with quiet, almost flat feet. These are proportion changes visible in the whole letter, not added detail.

Give the lower bays different curvature but comparable perceived area: the left rises a little higher; the right opens a little wider at its mouth. At twenty-four pixels, each mouth should retain at least three clear background pixels and each outside leg about four to five ink pixels. Avoid perfectly circular shoulder caps, uniform capsules and matching arch cutouts.

Rebuild the wordmark around the revised M, then narrow the l to about half the nominal monospace cell, widen the u's interior, blunt the v with the same controlled turn, and shorten the a's upper bowl while enlarging its lower counter. Preserve a clearly two-storey a and the l's identifying flag and foot. Reduce the M's mass to match the lowercase optical weight. The final prompts below describe this revised study; recognition and raster behavior still require visual verification.
logoPrompt: Create ONE final logo-only study for Mluva: a bold, soft, sculpted uppercase M monogram in a single connected mass of solid monochrome ink, color #111111, on ACTUAL transparent alpha. Output only the isolated M, centered with generous clear space. No wordmark, no other letters, no labels and no presentation sheet. The M is compact, about 1.06 times as wide as tall, with two substantial upright outer legs and nearly flat quiet feet. It must read unequivocally as a capital M at twenty-four pixels. The left shoulder is full-height and gently broad; the right shoulder is five percent lower and rolls into its side a little faster. Shoulders are deliberately shaped, never two identical round caps. A very deep open V-like cleft descends from the top between inclined sides, ending in a controlled rounded floor at fifty-eight percent of total height. The cleft axis sits at fifty-three percent of total width. Below that floor the diagonals meet in a softly blunted central join whose underside stops at eighty-two percent of total height, clearly above the feet. Leave two generous open background bays beneath the diagonals: left slightly taller, right slightly broader, comparable in perceived area. Each bay needs a broad visible mouth; avoid thin channels. Outside legs should read as four to five pixels of ink when the whole mark is twenty-four pixels wide. Shape the entire boundary as original filled artwork with confident changing curvature and firm structure. The effect is a voice rising and settling within a memorable initial, calm, tactile, immediate and quietly delightful. Use ONLY a flat opaque ink silhouette with real transparent background and transparent cutaway spaces. No strokes, outlines, microphone, speech bubble, tail, mouth, tooth, water, wave, droplet, bowtie, ribbon, ordinary corporate geometric M, stock rounded font, copied brand, gradient, glow, shadow, texture, three-dimensional render, app tile, border, checkerboard, backdrop, mockup or explanatory text.
wordmarkPrompt: Create ONE final wordmark-only study reading EXACTLY Mluva, uppercase M followed by lowercase luva, spelled without additions. Output only these five letters as flat solid monochrome ink #111111 on ACTUAL transparent alpha, horizontally arranged with generous surrounding clear space. No separate logo, symbol, tagline, label or layout sheet. Start from the legible upright filled letterforms of JetBrains Mono Medium, then substantially redraw them as coherent custom lettering. Preserve the practical typographic character and a clearly two-storey a. Give the M a broad sculpted skeleton, substantial upright outside legs, a deep central cleft with inclined sides and a controlled round floor, and a low blunted diagonal join that ends above the baseline. The M's left shoulder sits slightly higher and feels broader than the right; the central cleft and lower join share an axis slightly right of center. It must remain an unmistakable uppercase M. Reduce its mass relative to the standalone symbol so its optical weight matches luva. Make the l about half a nominal monospace cell wide, preserving a modest identifying head flag and a short rightward foot. Widen the u's interior and give its bottom a generous controlled turn. Keep the v decisively diagonal, with a short softly blunted bottom related to the M join; do not turn it into a second u. Shorten the a's upper bowl and enlarge its lower counter while retaining its two-storey skeleton and clear right stem. Design counter spaces and turning curves as one family. This must be noticeably customized lettering, beyond a stock font with rounded corners. Use compact optical spacing, careful M–l balance and clear separation of all five letters; no ligatures or overlaps. Keep one shared baseline and restrained readable lowercase proportions. All visible forms are filled opaque ink and all surrounding space and counters are truly transparent. No outlines, strokes, detached dots, speech tails, microphone, gradient, glow, shadows, three-dimensional effects, texture, app tile, checkerboard, background, mockup or text other than Mluva.
smallSizeRisks: The central cleft can become shallow after rasterization and suggest lowercase m; inspect its depth at twenty-four pixels before judging the large artwork.
The two lower bays can close near their upper ends; preserve at least three clear pixels across each mouth at twenty-four pixels and judge their visible depth in both ink and reversed use.
Too much mass in the center can create a third foot or tooth reading; keep its underside visibly above the baseline and inspect the silhouette without accompanying lettering.
Five-percent shoulder asymmetry may rasterize differently on adjacent pixel grids. The M must remain balanced and legible even when that nuance is reduced.
The customized wordmark's l flag and a upper counter need separate small-text review. Prefer the standalone M when the five-letter name cannot retain those distinctions.
opticalRules: Construct one connected filled silhouette. Negative space is open background, with no applied white shapes that would fail on another surface.
Use a width-to-height ratio near 1.06. Deepen the top cleft to about 58 percent of height and end the center at about 82 percent; both share an axis at about 53 percent of width.
Keep the right shoulder roughly 5 percent lower than the left. Optical balance takes priority over exact arithmetic after raster review.
Keep outside feet nearly level and broad, with softened corner turns. Neither the central join nor any decorative projection reaches their baseline.

At a twenty-four-pixel mark width, target four to five pixels of ink in each outer leg and at least three clear pixels at each lower bay's mouth. These are drawing targets, not validated measurements.
Use full-opacity ink or a full-opacity reversed light silhouette. Adjust the reversed master only if pixel review reveals visible counter loss; do not introduce outline compensation.
Give the standalone mark clear space of at least one outer-leg width. Evaluate it without a tile or lockup before evaluating composed use.
Keep the wordmark's exact Mluva spelling, the l's flag and foot, and the a's two-storey construction. Match optical weight rather than copying the standalone M's density.
Preserve the JetBrains Mono provenance and OFL notice in any later outlined artwork implementation; this study does not modify font binaries or production assets.
motionRelationship: The final M can share the existing film's calm pacing and the breathing study's 3.4-second cadence without becoming a liquid surface. In an optional motion study, hold the feet and central axis stationary while the two shoulders expand outward by at most one percent of the mark's width, with the right shoulder following slightly later. Keep both lower openings and the deep cleft readable throughout; never morph into a waveform, stretch the center into a tail or animate the shape as an audio-level meter. A short, quiet appearance followed by a long readable hold is sufficient for the title and closing frames. The mark stays flat opaque ink while the film's licensed water remains a separate background element. Reduced motion uses the complete static silhouette immediately. These are art-direction options for the study, not a change to recording status or a promise of provider latency.
